sections.h2: What is Hart County, Georgia, and who handles its property tax?
sections.html:
Hart County is a lake county in northeast Georgia along the I-85 corridor. Hartwell is the county seat, Lake Hartwell supplies 222 miles of shoreline, and Exit 177 on I-85 is about an hour and a half from Atlanta. The Census Bureau lists 232 square miles of land and a 2025 population estimate of 28,639.

Hart County was formed in 1853 from parts of Elbert and Franklin counties and is the only Georgia county named for a woman, the Revolutionary War figure Nancy Hart. Gateway Industrial Park sits at the I-85 exit, and the county shares an airport and an animal shelter with Franklin County. The county's own profile cites about 49 inches of rain a year, with summer averages near 89 degrees and winter averages near 57, which is the climate any buyer's inspector will be reading a house against.

  • Board of Tax Assessors: P.O. Box 810, Hartwell, GA 30643, 706-376-3997. Values property, takes homestead applications and handles appeals.
  • Tax Commissioner: in the courthouse in Hartwell. Collects property tax, auto tags, timber payments, mobile home tax and the intangible recording tax.
  • Records: the county website links to a property tax record search and to an online payment site.

sections.h2: When are Hart County property taxes due?
sections.html:
The county's assessment page says taxes are normally due by December 20 each year, but state law gives taxpayers 60 days from the date of mailing before interest may be charged. In practice, the date on your own bill is the one that controls.

Georgia's revenue department puts it the same way: December 20 is the official statewide due date, a county can move it to December 1 or November 15, and a bill carries a 60 day grace from the postmark. Penalties can attach to delinquent taxes on top of interest. Hart County's tax commissioner has added a drop box outside the courthouse for property and auto payments, and an online payment option is linked from the county website.

Mobile homes follow a separate schedule. Owners of a mobile home located in Hart County on January 1 must return it for taxation with the Tax Commissioner on or before May 1, and the annual location permit is also due between January 1 and May 1. A new permit is required within 30 days of permanent placement. Check with the Tax Commissioner for the bill due date on a mobile home account.

sections.h2: How do I challenge a Hart County assessment?
sections.html:
Mail the appeal to the Board of Tax Assessors, postmarked no later than 45 days from the date of the change of assessment notice. The county's page says that when assessors disagree with your returned value, they change it and send the notice.

Hart County states that every parcel is reevaluated each year, and a tax notice is sent out each year by April 15. Owners in Hartwell and on the lake shore should read that notice as soon as it arrives, because the 45 day appeal clock starts from the notice date. The assessors' office will explain the filing procedure by phone.

Another route runs through the return. Property tax returns may be filed with the assessors between January 1 and April 1. The tax commissioner's page tells owners who think their value is too high to file a return reducing it by April 1 in order to have a chance at a lower value for the next year's taxes. Georgia's revenue department adds that a refund claim for tax that was erroneously or illegally collected must begin within three years of payment, in writing to the county governing authority.

sections.h2: What homestead and exemption rules apply in Hart County?
sections.html:
A homestead filer must live in the home, and it must be the filer's legal residence. Hart County says the application is filed with the tax assessor's office. A person away for health reasons will not be denied, and a family member or friend can notify the office on their behalf.

  • To receive the exemption for the current tax year, you must have owned the property on January 1 and filed by the date returns are due, which is April 1.
  • Certain elderly owners qualify for additional exemptions beyond the regular homestead. The Tax Commissioner's page says to apply by April 1 of each year to receive them in future years.
  • Ask the assessors at 706-376-3997 whether any local homestead exemption applies to your parcel on top of the state ones.

For a seller, the timing matters in the year of the sale. A buyer who moves in after January 1 files for their own exemption the next season, and a seller who has moved out should not expect to keep the old one. Georgia's revenue department says that failing to apply counts as a waiver.

sections.h2: What do the Census numbers show for Hart County housing?
sections.html:
Hart County is affordable by Georgia standards. The Census Bureau QuickFacts table puts the median owner-occupied home at $215,100 for 2020 to 2024, the median gross rent at $844, and the homeownership rate at 77.8%.

The county grew 10.9% from the April 2020 base to the 2025 estimate. Roughly one resident in four is 65 or older. With 13,800 housing units against 11,034 households, the county has more homes than households. Owners of a house that sits empty part of the year can ask the Tax Commissioner and the assessors whether any exemption they hold still applies.

sections.h2: What should a Hart County seller know about recording and closing costs?
sections.html:
Hart County's Tax Commissioner collects the intangible recording tax. Every holder of a long-term note secured by real estate must record the security instrument in the county where the property sits within 90 days, and the tax is $1.50 for each $500 of the face amount or fraction of it.

A seller mostly needs the property tax payoff and a clean title. The county homepage lists 185 West Franklin Street in Hartwell as the overnight and physical address for the Clerk of Superior Court, who handles recording, and it notes that mail to the office had been coming back from the post office.

Before listing a Hart County house, gather your latest assessment notice, the most recent tax bill, any mobile home permit records and any covenant paperwork. Ask the Tax Commissioner for the unpaid balance and ask the closing attorney who will carry the current year's bill, since the contract decides how it is split.

faqs.q: When are Hart County property taxes due?
faqs.a: The county says taxes are normally due by December 20, and state law gives 60 days from the mailing date before interest can be charged. Use the date on your bill as the final answer.

faqs.q: How long do I have to appeal a Hart County assessment?
faqs.a: The appeal must be sent to the Board of Tax Assessors and postmarked within 45 days of the date on the change of assessment notice. Call 706-376-3997 for the filing procedure.

faqs.q: When is the Hart County homestead exemption deadline?
faqs.a: April 1. You must have owned and lived in the home on January 1 and file with the tax assessor's office by the date returns are due.

faqs.q: Where do I pay a Hart County mobile home tax?
faqs.a: Pay the Tax Commissioner. The mobile home return and location permit are due between January 1 and May 1, and the owner of a mobile home in the county on January 1 is the one who files.

faqs.q: Does Hart County reassess every year?
faqs.a: Yes. The county states that every parcel is reevaluated each year, and a tax notice goes out by April 15. File an appeal within 45 days of the notice date if you disagree.
